html:
Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza was an Italian-born French explorer who claimed the lands north of the Congo river for France in the 1870s and 1880s.

Travelling up the Ogooué from Libreville and on to the Congo, he made treaties with local rulers, above all the Makoko of the Tio, usually without force. He became the first commissioner general of French Congo.

He was dismissed in 1898, and the colony was handed to concession companies that brutalised workers for rubber and ivory. Sent back in 1905 to investigate abuses, he died at Dakar on the way home, and his report was suppressed. In 2006 his remains were moved to a mausoleum in Brazzaville, the only African capital still named after a colonist, a choice that has drawn criticism. His name is also tied to French Equatorial Africa.
